h: The Stillness of Shabbos Welcomes the Divine King

p: יוּבַן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת נח, א)
This can be understood from what is stated in the Gemara (Berachos 58a):
and there was a din, etc.;
the king is not coming, etc.
Surely now the king is coming, etc.
is like the kingship of Heaven,
Hashem is not in the wind, etc.;
Hashem is not in the earthquake, etc.;
Hashem is not in the fire;
Now the three days before Shabbos
and the three days after Shabbos
and as they said, of blessed memory (end of Chagigah, 27a):
corresponding to the middah of Yaakov,
And in the six days of work
it is the aspect of the still, small voice,
and one need not do anything,
And this is what the Arizal composed
"And it is not a noisy matter";
for on Shabbos one does not need
for it is in the aspect of the still, small voice.
And even what they said, of blessed memory
who during the six days of work
is in the aspect of the still, small voice.
during the six days of work
and with all these three middos
for the whole strength of Shabbos
is at the time it begins to depart;
and then it is in the aspect of
But it must also be with joy,
And it says (in Tanna Devei Eliyahu, chapter 3):
"My fear is from within my joy,
and my joy is from within my fear":
for at first one must be in joy,
and the dread before Him, blessed be His Name;
and afterward he is in greater joy,
the yirah to him more and more.
And this is "for the King comes,"
